selection: smallest-haystack per question_type — selection bias toward easier questions (caveat)
v3_changes_over_v2: Compress prompt: added explicit '## AssistantRecommendations' section to capture facts from the assistant side of the conversation (fixes v2's q5 snapper miss where the answer was an assistant-recommended dish, not a user-stated fact)
Anti-leak preamble: strict deny-list, 'if uncertain, omit', no meta-acknowledgments, recency reminder at end of prompt

RAW improved 0→1/3 — stronger isolation prompt helps engagement. COMPACT preserved.

v2_vs_v3_pooled.interpretation: v3 raised the floor (raw 19→39%) more than the ceiling (compact 57→61%). The stricter isolation prompt cured the over-refusal habit in raw long-context Q&A. Compact gains came from fixing q5 (assistant turn capture); other compact wins were already strong.

memory_leak_v3.interpretation: Down from v2's ~15%. Still nonzero — subagent system prompt is sticky despite explicit deny-list. Persistent ~10-15% is a Workflow subagent property, not a prompt problem.

compression_ratio_v3: ~20x typical (118K -> 5-7K tokens). Larger than v2's 30x because the added ## AssistantRecommendations section grows the digest.
key_insights: Strong isolation prompt is dual-edged: helps BOTH conditions. Raw improved more because it was suffering from systematic over-refusal — the prompt 'use ONLY this context' makes raw more willing to engage with the long haystack instead of bouncing to 'context does not contain answer'.

Compact's edge comes from STRUCTURED PRESENTATION, not added information. When raw refuses, compact answers correctly using the same content. Pattern visible on q3 (3/3 vs 0/3 even at v3): compact AI connects 'Holiday Market = week before Black Friday' + 'iPhone = on Black Friday' from adjacent digest lines.

Compress agent can lose needles. q0 painting: digest captured 'flea market find worth triple' but lost the 'sunset painting' linkage. Compression has a recall-precision tradeoff — small details get folded into larger categories.
Q5 fix proves prompt-level corrections work: just adding ## AssistantRecommendations flipped q5 from 0/3 to 2/3. Future digest schema iterations could fix q0 (add ## OwnershipAndValuation section).
Memory contamination is intrinsic to Workflow subagents at ~10-15% rate — even after explicit deny-listing the markers. To get to 0%, need a different agent type OR claude -p headless route.

comparison_to_published.caveat: Not directly comparable. (a) Our n=18 vs their n=500. (b) We sampled smallest haystack per type. (c) Opus 4.7 is a different runner than what published baselines used — our raw at 39% suggests Opus has a more conservative refusal habit than the model behind the 60.2% Full-Context baseline. To enter the leaderboard properly we need the full 500 with random sampling.

what_v3_proves: Methodology is solid: anti-leak, sequential cycling, plain-text VERDICT parsing all work. Token budget is manageable ($0 on subscription, ~10M tokens total for the v3 sweep).
Compact mode adds measurable value: 11/18 vs 7/18, +22pp pooled.

The mdfy /raw/hub/<slug>?digest=1&compact=1 endpoint claim — that compression preserves answer-finding — has directional evidence on a small sample. Strong enough for internal product confidence, weak for external publishing.
what_v3_does_not_prove: Pure 'cross-AI parity' claim (we only tested Opus 4.7).
Comparable position vs memory.inc / Mastra / Supermemory — those numbers were on full set with their own setups.

tier_1_cheap_high_value: Switch from Workflow agent() to `claude -p` headless. Eliminates the ~10% memory leak entirely. ~2 hour build time.
Random sampling instead of smallest-per-type. Currently selection bias toward easy questions; fix is one-line code change but requires args-passing rework (workflow script size cap).
tier_2_real_investment: Run full LongMemEval-S 500 with v3 methodology. Token budget ~150M, wall time ~10 hr on subscription with TPM-respecting pacing. Output: headline numbers we can publish.
Add a third runner (Sonnet 4.6) within the workflow for cross-model comparison. Tests 'cross-AI parity' claim directly.
tier_3_research: Build a 'digest schema' optimizer: iterate which markdown sections capture the most facts per token. q0 painting needs an ## OwnershipAndValuation section. q5 needed ## AssistantRecommendations. There's a fixed schema design problem here.
Variance reduction: N=10 instead of N=3 for the questions where compact margin is small (q1 antiques). Cleaner signal on borderline cases.
